task.title: Refuse newer-writer packs with an upgrade signal instead of corrupt-data
task.description:
From v0.5.0 on, readers should distinguish 'this history was written by a newer workbook' from 'this history is corrupt.' Today any pack using semantics an older build cannot fold is reported as corrupt-data (measured on v0.4.4: a custom-status pack blocks the ref at fetch time forever; a restore-into pack reads fine but fails validate permanently, per the PR #95 review record). Installed binaries are frozen, but v0.5.0 is unreleased — teaching it the signal now makes this the last hard edge.

Design direction (agreed 2026-08-13): operation packs (task and config ledger) carry a writer-format marker ONLY when they use semantics older readers cannot fold — a minimum-reader version, bumped deliberately per breaking change; its absence means 'foldable by v0.5.0', so no pack any current build writes changes by a byte (byte-compat golden required). A reader encountering a marker above its own version — including an unrecognized operation type under such a marker — refuses with a distinct category and a message telling the user to upgrade workbook, scoped like today's refusals (per task / per ledger), never wedging sync or holding back other refs; validate reports the same way.

First consumer: the comments/attachments story (WB-01KYD77EV9XVA1K0KBY2561GGC) ships new operation types that must carry the marker; that story depends on this one.
